newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG says up to 23 missing after storms at sea.
newsitem.headline: PNG says up to 23 missing after storms at sea.

text.p: Cyclonic weather has killed two people in Papua New Guinea and left as many as 23 missing at sea, emergency officials said on Wednesday.

Cyclone Justin off the northeast coast of Australia was whipping up rough seas and gale force winds in Papua New Guinea, Australia's nearest northern neighbour, said Leith Anderson, head of the National Disaster and Emergency Services.
The cyclone is hovering over the Coral Sea about 600 kms (370 miles) south of Papua New Guinea.
Anderson said two people had been killed by falling coconut trees, two others were confirmed missing at sea after a barge capsized and a further 21 are believed missing at sea.
"I am trying to confirm that they (the 21) are missing," Anderson told Reuters.
"The problem here is that we have a lot of people moving about in boats and they may be just sheltering on an island and pop up once things die down," he said.
Anderson said reports from New Britain island said 11 people in one boat had gone missing west of the island and another boat with 10 people had gone missing off the island's east coast.
Cyclone Justin, which has been downgraded to category one of a five-point cyclone scale, was exacerbating Papua New Guinea's monsoonal weather, Anderson said.

"The weather here is absolutely terrible," he said. "We have wind gusts around 64 kph (40 mph) in Port Moresby and waves are breaking over the reef that runs along the town. It's the most impressive display of weather I have seen here in 23 years."
Cyclone Justin stretches over an area of about 1,000 km (620 miles) and is sitting about 650 km (400 miles) east of Cairns on the Australian east coast.
The cyclone, the largest to appear along Australia's east coast for 20 years, is stationary with winds at its epicentre of up to 100 kph (62 mph)
